messages.author: 7324f87aaa1afb0b
messages.subject: IC=HSCV for low quality data
parts:
Hi Chris,

After the webinar I compared using HSCV and AICc as the IC within ctmm.select() as you suggested after hearing about what I have seen with some models that included a 3m error term within GUESS. I did not explore IC=LOOCV as my goal for these analyses is to derive a home range. Using HSCV seems promising. But I did notice that after fitting movement models and attempting to extract the top model, the extracted model was not what was listed first in the summary of candidate models. For instance, the following eight models extracted for an individual do not match the sequence seen in the summary.

 

#1[1] "OU isotropic error"

#2[1] "OUf isotropic error"

#3[1] "OUF isotropic error"

#4 [1] "IID isotropic error"

#5[1] "OUF anisotropic error"

#6[1] "BM isotropic error"

#7[1] "OUF anisotropic error"

#8[1] "BM isotropic error"

 

Models in the summary are listed by AIC but that is not the information criterion used with HSCV, so I'm wondering if that has something to do with this. If what I'm seeing is correct, is it appropriate to use the first model extracted from the candidate set regardless of what order is shown in the summary? For many individuals IID was the extracted model with topmodel <- FIT[[1]] but it did not appear first in the summary. I could usually get another movement model as the "top" model if I fiddled with GUESS enough. If the second extracted model is a relatively good fit, would it be better to go with that over IID? Thanks as always for the guidance!

Ross

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: IC=HSCV for low quality data
parts:
Hi Ross,

summary() has an IC argument that is "AICc" by default, like ctmm.select(), so try summary(FITS,IC="HSCV") in that case.

I will see if I can add an IC attribute to ctmm.select() output so that summary() can detect what IC was originally used by ctmm.select().

Best,
Chris
